contributions: Introduces AGENTMERCURY as a scenario-grounded framework for synthesizing executable environments with an explicit PLANET role for world construction
Constructs and releases 4,783 executable business environments spanning 14 industries and 50 countries
Shows policies trained on these environments improve on both in-domain enterprise workflows and out-of-domain benchmarks despite no task overlap
Demonstrates that construction traces can teach models to author executable worlds, improving success from 3.3% to 83.3%
Releases environments, tasks, construction code, and trained models
limitations: The paper notes that existing environments are typically task-centric and optimized for specific tasks rather than representing broader scenarios; however, this is framed as a motivation rather than a limitation of AGENTMERCURY itself. No explicit limitations of AGENTMERCURY are stated in the provided text.
methods: AGENTMERCURY separates environment construction from agent interaction via a PLANET role that transforms high-level business scenarios into executable worlds containing entities, services, tools, persistent state, and cross-service invariants with executable verification conditions. Tasks are then instantiated from the constructed world rather than used to define it. Policies are trained via reinforcement learning directly in these environments, and construction traces are used as structured supervision to fine-tune a model for environment authoring.
results: 4,783 executable environments were synthesized across 14 industries and 50 countries. Qwen3.5-4B improved from 12.3 to 15.7 on EnterpriseOps-GYM and from 45.9 to 56.0 on AIME26 after training on AGENTMERCURY environments. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on construction traces increased executable-world authoring success from 3.3% to 83.3% on held-out business scenarios.
tldr: AGENTMERCURY is a scalable framework that synthesizes executable business environments from high-level scenarios, separating world construction from task specification so agents can learn in diverse, persistent worlds.
